module: In-house 2D polygon booleans (union, difference), Martinez-like, adapted from the polybooljs approach (MIT). A polygon is a table { regions = { ring, ... }, inverted = bool } where each ring is a list of {x,y} points. Computations are done in a local frame near the origin so that the absolute epsilon does not get crushed at world coordinates. areas then sorts a list of rings into outer rings with their holes, ready for triangulation.
usage:
local pb = extensions.editor_toolUtilities_polyBool
local res = pb.difference(terrainRing, roadRing)
for _, a in ipairs(pb.areas(res.regions)) do
  -- a.ring (CCW), a.holes (list of CW rings)
end
notes: difference accepts flexible input: { regions }, a single ring, or a list of rings; points can be {x=,y=} or {[1],[2]}.
unionMany, in contrast, expects tables with the regions field (and inverted) for each element.
Rings of fewer than 3 points are ignored. If the clip is empty, difference returns the subject as is.
Internal tolerances: eps 1e-10 for the sweep, SNAP 1e-6 for the input grid, WELD 1e-4 to weld nearly coincident corners.

unionMany.desc: Merges several polygons into one. Returns an empty polygon if the list is empty.

polys.desc: List of polygons { regions = {ring,...}, inverted = bool }.

returns.desc: Result polygon { regions, inverted } in world coordinates.

difference.desc: Boolean difference: subject minus clip. Works in a local frame like unionMany.

subject.desc: Polygon, ring or list of rings to subtract from.

clip.desc: Polygon, ring or list of rings to subtract.

areas.desc: Sorts the flat list of rings of a boolean result into outer rings each carrying their holes. Nesting is deduced from containment depth: even = solid, odd = hole. Outer rings oriented CCW, holes CW. Each hole is attached to the deepest ring that contains it.

regions.desc: List of {x,y} rings (e.g. result.regions from difference).

returns.desc: List of { ring = ring, holes = { ring, ... } }.
